chunks: And everything in it (the book) that is narrated from Zakariyya ibn Malik Al-Jufi, I have transmitted it from Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris - may Allah have mercy on him - from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Abu Al-Abbas Al-Fadl ibn Abdul Malik, from Zakariyya ibn Malik Al-Jufi.

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris, a key narrator in the chain transmitted by Shaykh al-Saduq.
key_terms.رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: May Allah have mercy on him, a common honorific used for deceased scholars and narrators.
key_terms.زَكَرِيَّا بْنِ مَالِكٍ الْجَعْفِيِّ: Zakariyya ibn Malik Al-Jufi, a prominent companion of the Imams whose narrations are central to this text.
key_terms.صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى: Safwan ibn Yahya, a well-known companion of Imam al-Sadiq and Imam al-Kazim, appearing in the chain.

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain for narrations from Zakariyya ibn Malik in Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage functions as a critical colophon in *Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih*, establishing a unified *isnad* (transmission chain) for all narrations attributed to Zakariyya ibn Malik Al-Jufi, thereby ensuring textual consistency and authenticity. By tracing the lineage through prominent figures like Ibn Idris and Safwan ibn Yahya, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the reliability of the Kufan scholarly tradition and provides readers with a clear methodological framework for verifying the hadiths.
